name: Codebuff

surfaces.label: Codebuff CLI (npm `codebuff`, bins `codebuff` and `cb`). The npm bin is only a Node launcher (`node .../codebuff/index.js`); it downloads a Bun-compiled binary to ~/.config/manicode/codebuff and spawns it with argv[0] = that full path. Match the binary, never the launcher (argv[0] is `node`). The same binary re-executes itself with --terminal-command-broker for every shell tool call; that helper is excluded here and is the working signal instead.

Freebuff CLI (npm `freebuff`, bin `freebuff`). Same source tree and same launcher as Codebuff, built with FREEBUFF_MODE=true; binary ~/.config/manicode/freebuff. Shares ~/.config/manicode with Codebuff.

Freebuff Desktop (Electron, com.freebuff.desktop). Matched on the local orchestrator that Freebuff.app starts as `Contents/Resources/bun/bun Contents/Resources/orchestrator/orchestrator.js`, one per app, hosting every thread of every open project. NOT matched on the Electron main process (Contents/MacOS/Freebuff), whose Chromium helpers would look like tool children. It also spawns claude and codex CLIs as children (harness choice per thread), which match the claude-code and codex rows: drop those by ancestry.
Freebuff Web, Cloud and Chat (hosted, no local process)

working_signals.name: codebuff
working_signals.meaning: Codebuff CLI only, only while a shell tool call runs: the binary re-executes itself (`<same path> --terminal-command-broker`, detached) as a DIRECT child and that helper runs `bash -c <cmd>` under it. Absent while the model streams or files are edited. Counts only as a direct child of the matched process. Do not apply the generic rule 'ignore a child with the same executable as its parent' to this row. Not present during a sponsored (ads) run, which uses a sandbox broker instead.

working_signals.name: freebuff
working_signals.meaning: Same as above for the Freebuff CLI: direct child `freebuff --terminal-command-broker` while a shell tool call runs.

working_signals.name: bash
working_signals.meaning: Freebuff Desktop orchestrator: it runs shell tool calls itself with no broker, so `bash -c <cmd>` is a direct child of the bun process while the command runs. Also true for a CLI turn that runs as a sponsored (ads) run: the SDK then uses a sandbox broker and the shell is a direct child of the CLI [inferred: sandbox-exec execs its target]. Weak, three known false positives: (1) Desktop's embedded terminal panel spawns the user's interactive login shell (`$SHELL -l`, or `bash --rcfile ... -i`) as a direct child of the orchestrator for as long as the panel is open, so SHELL=/bin/bash reads as permanently working (zsh, the macOS default, does not match this name); (2) a project startup script runs as `bash -lc <script>` for up to 120 s when a thread is set up; (3) nothing distinguishes these by name, and the schema has no argument filter for child_process.

CLI: a run checkpoints its chat at start (the prompt) and then the SDK calls onStateSnapshot on a 5 s timer, but a tick is skipped unless the run's messageHistory array was replaced since the last tick (a step boundary: model reply finished, tool result added). The CLI then rewrites run-state.json and chat-messages.json (plus chat-meta.json) in the chat directory, and a synchronous save happens at turn end; log.jsonl is appended too. So writes come at most every 5 s and NOT during one long model call or one long tool call. Raises working, never lowers it. A process maps to a chat directory only by cwd basename (or --continue <id>), and the directory changes on /new and /history.
Fallback. Unmeasured guess (nothing was running). The CLI is a Bun OpenTUI renderer with ad polling; idle CPU is unknown.

waiting_signals.meaning: CLI: no hook, notification command, bell, OSC progress or power assertion. Blocked-on-human states are TUI-only: the ask_user form (askUserState), the .agents trust prompt, login, and the Freebuff waiting-room queue. No tool-approval prompt for shell commands was found in cli/src. The terminal title is set to the typed input, not a state.

Freebuff Desktop only, weak: raised for `failed`, `merge-conflict` and `auto-stopped`; these mean look at me, not a permission or question. Pending questions and permission requests were not found in the schema (tables: projects, threads, messages, queue_items, auto_run_decision_receipts, sponsored_runs, thread_deliveries), so they are probably in memory only [inferred].

hooks.config: None. Neither the CLI nor Desktop reads a hooks config. `run_file_change_hooks` is a tool the agent calls (a no-op in the SDK), not a lifecycle hook. Nearest equivalents: custom agents in .agents/ (TypeScript) and, in Desktop, per-thread state in .freebuff/desktop-v2.db.

telemetry.how: No OpenTelemetry exporter in cli/, sdk/, common/ or agents/ (grep for opentelemetry, OTEL_, otlp hits only bun.lock, where it is an optional peer of next). Product analytics go to PostHog and logs to an Axiom sink via /api/logs. Desktop app.asar has no otlp string; its orchestrator bundle contains @opentelemetry/api and OTEL_* names only because it bundles the Claude Agent SDK for the claude harness.

sources.claim: Every shell tool call on the CLI goes through a broker: the CLI spawns process.execPath with --terminal-command-broker (detached, env CODEBUFF_TERMINAL_COMMAND_BROKER=1); that helper spawns the command (`bash -c <command>` on POSIX) as its own child and reaps its process group when done. So the direct child is the same executable, and bash is a grandchild. Exception: a sponsored (ads) turn passes createSponsoredCodeSearchBroker instead, so the shell runs under /usr/bin/sandbox-exec (direct child, expected to exec into bash)
sources.evidence: cli/src/utils/terminal-command-broker.ts defaultBrokerInvocation (line 340-353), createTerminalCommandBroker.start, serveTerminalCommandBroker; cli/src/entry.ts (dispatch on the flag); cli/src/utils/codebuff-client.ts line 97 passes terminalCommandBroker; sdk/src/tools/run-terminal-command.ts lines 395-396 shell = 'bash', shellArgs = ['-c']; CodebuffAI/codebuff at commit 97654d3e69e37bdca502ce2dcf131e69730fd3c4 (2026-09-29, shallow clone, the repo now redirects to CodebuffAI/freebuff); sponsored exception: cli/src/utils/sponsored-run.ts line 1565 (processBroker = createSponsoredCodeSearchBroker) and line 1735 (terminalCommandBroker: processBroker); sdk/src/tools/sponsored-sandbox.ts darwin arm uses /usr/bin/sandbox-exec; Desktop orchestrator.js spawnMac at ~line 132968. That sandbox-exec execs its target is inferred, not observed. Re-verified against the shipped 1.0.688 binary (see the binary-strings source)

notes: One codebase, three local products. CLI: the process to watch is the Bun binary in ~/.config/manicode, not the npm launcher. The Codebuff and Freebuff CLIs share the store, so the store cannot say which wrote a chat; the process can. A CLI process holds exactly one chat at a time but rotates it on /new and /history, and the store folder is the cwd basename, so map a process to a chat by cwd plus newest mtime and treat it as a guess unless --continue <id> was on the command line. Working signals for the CLI are weak by design: a broker child (same executable, --terminal-command-broker) during shell tool calls, and chat-file rewrites every ~5 s during a run; model streaming without files changing is invisible. Do not use tool_children here: a permanent /bin/sh watchdog child would mark every idle CLI working. Freebuff Desktop is different: one orchestrator process hosts every thread, and the exact answer is threads.turn_state = 'running' in <project>/.freebuff/desktop-v2.db (needs a new sqlite_row signal; read that column only, never messages.parts_json). Desktop threads can run claude and codex as children, so those match the claude-code and codex rows too and should be dropped by ancestry. Freebuff CLI has a waiting-room queue and session hours that are not a turn. Version researched: repo HEAD 97654d3 (2026-09-29), npm codebuff 1.0.688, freebuff 0.1.6, Desktop 0.0.152. Verification pass 2026-09-29 (second reader): the 5 s chat snapshot is skipped while the run waits on one slow model call (see the working_signals meaning), so the CLI's transcript signal can be quiet during a live turn; the `bash` child signal has known false positives on Desktop (embedded terminal with SHELL=bash, startup script) and is a weak signal there; a sponsored (ads) turn in the CLI or Desktop runs the shell through a sandbox broker, so the `codebuff --terminal-command-broker` child is absent then. The probe's session_id() returns whatever argv follows --continue, so `codebuff --continue --cwd X` or `codebuff --continue "prompt"` yields a junk id; harmless because no chat directory matches it, but do not treat it as a session id unless it looks like an ISO timestamp with ':' as '-'. Matching: names ['codebuff'] also catches a relocated binary (FREEBUFF_CONFIG_DIR) and any other executable named codebuff; the npm launcher, cb, the broker, the /bin/sh watchdog, the Bun probe (`bun --version`), the Electron main process and helpers, `tail codebuff.log` and the staged download `.codebuff-download-temp/codebuff` were run through matches(): only the staged download and a bare `/opt/homebrew/bin/codebuff` match (both tui; the launcher was not seen executing the staged copy). Never executed live: real ps output for every surface is still unseen.
